q: What makes up the carbon footprint of a tonne of copper cathode?
title: Copper cathode: footprint per tonne
short: Mining and concentrating ore, usually the largest share and heavy on diesel and electricity; smelting and converting; and electrolytic refining, which is mostly electricity. The grid behind the mine and refinery decides much of the total, so cathode from a coal heavy grid can carry several times the figure of cathode refined on clean power.
audience: Cable, wire and component makers buying copper, and their buyers asking for product footprints

ul: Mine: haul trucks, crushing and grinding, often the biggest part.

p: Cathode refined from scrap skips mining and concentrating, so its figure is usually much lower. Ask the supplier for the recycled share.
Ask your supplier for a cradle to gate figure with year and boundary. If you must use an average, name the source and mark it as an estimate.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so a copper product figure can be traced back to the documents behind it. Factors outside India are entered from the official source and labelled.
